# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 manufacturing and service firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| training_hours | Average annual training hours per employee, 2021-2022 |
| productivity_2023 | Value added per employee in 2023 (thousand USD) |
| log_employees_2020 | Log number of employees, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| productivity_2020 | Value added per employee in 2020, standardized |
| mgmt_rating_2023 | Management practices rating collected in 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| sector | Sector: manufacturing / services |
| export_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| family_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| rd_intensity_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| union_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| credit_score_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of employee training hours on firm productivity?

Approach: OLS of productivity_2023 on training_hours with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I focus on the north region subsample, where the data are most comparable, control for firm size, firm age and the pre-period value of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on training_hours is 0.091 (SE 0.404, p = 0.8214, N = 633).

Conclusion: no effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
d=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
pre='log_employees_2020+firm_age_2020+productivity_2020'
allc=pre+'+export_share_2020+foreign_owned+family_owned+rd_intensity_2020+union_share_2020+credit_score_2020+C(sector)+listed+C(region)'
for name,f,s in [('naive','productivity_2023~training_hours',d),('pre','productivity_2023~training_hours+'+pre,d),('all','productivity_2023~training_hours+'+allc,d),
 ('north','productivity_2023~training_hours+'+pre,d[d.region=='north'])]:
    r=smf.ols(f,s).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(name,len(s),r.params['training_hours'],r.bse['training_hours'],r.pvalues['training_hours'])
for g,s in d.groupby('region'):
    r=smf.ols('productivity_2023~training_hours+'+allc.replace('+C(region)',''),s).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(g,len(s),r.params['training_hours'],r.pvalues['training_hours'])

{"decision":"reject","reason":"The report restricts to the north region (N=633) with no stated justification and concludes 'no effect' from an insignificant, underpowered estimate (SE 0.40). On all 2000 firms, with the same pre-period controls, training_hours has a positive and significant coefficient (about 0.58, p≈0.012), and the result stays about the same with the full set of pre-period controls. A non-significant subsample result is not evidence of no effect."}

content.text:
I rejected the report's "no effect" conclusion, and `verdict.json` is written with that decision.

The analyst ran only the north region (about 630–650 firms) and gave no reason for choosing it. The coefficient there is small and imprecise (SE about 0.40), so a non-significant result says little. It doesn't show that training has no effect.

My re-runs on the full sample of 2,000 firms point the other way:

| Specification | Coefficient on training hours | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| No controls | 2.49 | below 0.001 |
| Size, age and 2020 productivity | 0.59 | 0.012 |
| Those plus all other pre-period controls, sector, listed status and region | 0.58 | 0.013 |

By region, with the full controls, the coefficients are 0.26 in the north (p about 0.54), 0.38 in central (p about 0.35) and 0.97 in the south (p about 0.012). The south estimate is significant and the other two are not. All three are positive.

My north-only run without the 1% trimming gave 0.24 (p about 0.58), against the report's 0.09. So the trimming and the exact sample also shift the number somewhat.

I did not use `mgmt_rating_2023` as a control. It was measured in 2023, after the training period.
